correctness.rationale: For each n>=4 and p in (0,1), the exact two-success binomial tail reduces the objective to H(j)=F(j)+F(n-j). Its first difference has a log-ratio with strictly negative second derivative on the half interval and zero at the midpoint; this proves edge-or-balanced-only extremizers. The edge-to-balance difference factors for even n and is p^2 times a one-sign-change polynomial for odd n; both have exactly one q root. The Poisson scaling of F proves n p_n -> 2.512862417... via a unique positive exponential root. Standard-library checker passed 1,693,847 exact-rational and numerical diagnostic assertions; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2009 and 2011 primary literature motivates the two-transit requirement and posterior-phase follow-up but does not establish the all-budget, two-ephemeris static allocation phase diagram. The closest indexed public three-session circle-arc theorem was read in full and cannot imply the arbitrary n two-discrete-hypothesis theorem without new reasoning; binomial increments and concavity are acknowledged as classical tools. Related resource allocation and binomial-tail records returned no exact or stronger coverage in inspected material. Unindexed broad allocation theorems are an explicit residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An older abstract or unindexed binomial-allocation theorem could already imply the edge-or-balanced property; relevant general resource allocation papers were not exhaustively read.
The ecological and astronomical relevance of the simplified two-mode independent-failure model is mathematical, not empirically validated.

value.rationale: A two-transit confirmation objective creates a nonconvex competition between concentrating uncertain observing phases and diversifying coverage. Exact all-budget endpoint/balance optimality, one finite transition per n, and a universal high-budget reliability product provide a reusable design benchmark, not a mere numerical instance, routine change of notation or tiny quantitative improvement. Its constraints and possible later need are explicit: two ephemeris aliases and sparse uncertain follow-up.
